name: Target Corporation
domainRelevance: Target operates ~1,950 stores across the U.S. with a discretionary-tilt merchandising mix (apparel, home, design collaborations) distinct from Walmart's consumables-heavy footprint. The "cheap chic" positioning via in-house brands (Cat & Jack, Good & Gather, Threshold) and designer partnerships (Missoni, Lilly Pulitzer) targets a slightly more affluent middle-income customer than Walmart's core. Post-2022 inventory miscalibration and 2024 boycott incidents created a structural reset in supply-chain discipline and promotional cadence.
portalRelevance: Target is a Level-2 peer in the mass-retail ecosystem and a critical functional node for understanding discretionary-apparel and home-goods demand signals. Its inventory-to-sales ratio, promotional intensity, and same-store sales trends serve as leading indicators for consumer confidence in non-essential categories. As a direct competitor to Walmart in urban/suburban markets and an indirect competitor to Amazon in discretionary e-commerce, Target's operational health and capital allocation decisions inform broader retail-sector risk assessment and supply-chain resilience modeling.

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Weekly comparable-store sales prints (disclosed in earnings releases and investor updates); apparel vs home category mix shifts
8-K filings for executive changes, material litigation, or supply-chain disruptions (e.g., 2024 boycott-related operational impacts)
Supplier price-change notices via EDI and quarterly gross-margin commentary in 10-Q; freight-cost pass-through dynamics
Inventory-to-sales ratio and days-inventory-outstanding trends; markdown velocity and promotional intensity signals

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Quarterly phase classification (p0–p10) based on OCF slope, revenue variance, and debt-coverage ratios; current state p6 (ORDER phase) indicates stabilized operations post-2023 reset
Rolling 4-quarter free-cash-flow trajectory and capital-allocation posture (buyback vs dividend vs debt reduction); Q1 2025 OCF slope +4.6% signals modest momentum
Inventory composition and turns by category (apparel, home, grocery); supply-chain lead-time normalization vs pre-pandemic baseline
Customer traffic (transactions) vs ticket (average transaction value) decomposition; discretionary-category penetration among income cohorts

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Pattern-match against prior P3/P7 transitions in SIC-5331 peer group (Kohl's, Bed Bath & Beyond); Target's 2022-23 inventory crisis mirrors Kohl's 2021-22 but with faster recovery trajectory
Gross-margin compression vs WMT and COST; apparel-mix leverage vs consumables-mix defensibility in recessionary scenarios
Promotional-intensity escalation as leading indicator of demand softness; markdown-rate acceleration in Q4 2024 vs Q4 2023 suggests consumer caution in discretionary
Supply-chain concentration risk:; freight-cost sensitivity to WTI and CNY FX

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: Inventory-throughput hedge via cotton futures and polyester-resin forwards to lock in apparel input costs; WTI-linked freight-cost collar to cap logistics inflation
Pricing-power buffer rebuild plan: maintain 50–75 bps gross-margin cushion to absorb tariff shocks or wage inflation without promotional escalation
Debt-maturity ladder stress-test under 300 bps+ interest-rate environment; maintain investment-grade rating (current: BBB+ S&P) via EBITDA/debt <2.5x
Antitrust monitoring: FTC scrutiny of private-label expansion (Cat & Jack, Good & Gather) vs national-brand shelf-space allocation; ensure compliance with UDAP standards

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Board-approved $5B share-repurchase authorization (disclosed in 2024 proxy); execute at TGT <$75/share to maximize EPS accretion
Dividend policy: maintain $0.90/share annual payout (3.5% yield at $25 price); pause increase if OCF growth stalls or debt-to-EBITDA exceeds 2.8x
Supply-chain diversification: expand Vietnam + India sourcing to 35% of apparel volume (from ) to reduce China tariff exposure
Category-mix rebalancing: grow grocery penetration to 25% of sales (from ~20%) via expanded Good & Gather and fresh-food partnerships; reduce apparel mix volatility

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 same-store sales validation: track apparel vs home category comps; flag if apparel comp <-2% for two consecutive quarters as demand-destruction signal
Share-price reaction to inventory disclosure: monitor TGT vs WMT relative performance on inventory-to-sales beats/misses; 200+ bps underperformance = structural concern
Gross-margin trend vs guidance: compare actual gross-margin rate to management guidance; 25+ bps miss signals promotional pressure or input-cost pass-through failure
Debt-rating agency commentary: track S&P, Moody's, Fitch outlooks for rating-action triggers (e.g., debt-to-EBITDA >3.0x, OCF decline >10% YoY)

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Seasonality reweighting in kernel snapshot: Q4 apparel-mix surge (30%+ of annual) vs Q1-Q3 flattening; adjust phase-transition thresholds for holiday-driven inventory builds
Supplier-concentration sensitivity recalibration: if Vietnam sourcing >40% of apparel, increase tariff-shock scenario weight in stress-test; monitor geopolitical risk to ASEAN supply
Promotional-intensity elasticity update: if markdown rate >18% of sales (vs historical 15%), lower gross-margin assumption by 50 bps in forward projections
Competitor-response modeling: if WMT apparel penetration exceeds 22% of WMT sales (from ), increase TGT market-share-loss probability in discretionary categories

functionalNetwork.model: Target Corporation operates as a mini-brain within the mass-retail ecosystem, with sensory inputs from supplier price signals and consumer-demand indices, motor outputs via inventory and promotional decisions, and salience nodes monitoring regulatory and competitive threats. Each functional-network entry carries both a neuralRole (DMN, Sensory, Motor, Salience, Limbic, PFC, Peer) and a specific brainNodeId from the canonical 124-node taxonomy, enabling pattern transfer across business structure and neural organization. The company's discretionary-tilt merchandising mix (apparel, home, design collaborations) creates distinct supplier dependencies and customer-demand sensitivities compared to Walmart's consumables-heavy model, requiring separate state-estimation and diagnosis pathways.

suppliers.name: The Procter & Gamble Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: PG supplies beauty (Olay, Pantene, SK-II), household (Tide, Dawn, Febreze), and personal-care SKUs across Target's beauty and household categories. 2018 beauty-reset partnership elevated premium tiers (Olay Regenerist, Pantene Gold Series) to anchor positions. Target's Up & Up private-label benchmark directly shapes PG's value-tier pricing strategy. Estimated 8–10% of Target's beauty + household sales; disclosed in 10-K Item 1A supplier concentration.

suppliers.name: The Coca-Cola Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: KO premium-tier SKUs (Smartwater, Topo Chico, Body Armor, Minute Maid) overweight at Target vs Walmart due to Target's discretionary-friendly customer mix and higher-income store locations. Target carries expanded cold-brew and functional-beverage assortment vs WMT's price-focused SKU set. Estimated 6–8% of Target beverage sales; Q3 2024 earnings call highlighted premium-beverage growth outpacing value-tier.

suppliers.name: Mondelez International
suppliers.relationshipNote: MDLZ supplies Oreo, Ritz, Cadbury, Trident across Target's grocery and confectionery aisles. Smaller share of Target sales (~4–5%) than at Walmart due to Target's smaller grocery footprint per store and higher-margin private-label snack penetration (Good & Gather). 2024 pricing actions on Oreo and Ritz created margin pressure; Target absorbed via promotional markdown rather than EDLP pass-through.

suppliers.name: Nike Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Nike supplies footwear, apparel, and accessories across Target's activewear and casual-wear categories. Target carries Nike basics and value-tier (Nike Dri-FIT, Revolution) below Foot Locker and Dick's Sporting Goods premium positioning. Estimated 3–4% of Target apparel sales. 2023-24 inventory reset included Nike SKU rationalization; Target reduced low-turn SKUs and focused on core basics. Nike's direct-to-consumer shift reduced wholesale allocation; Target negotiated volume commitments to maintain shelf space.

suppliers.name: Hasbro Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Hasbro supplies toys (Transformers, Marvel, Nerf, Play-Doh) and entertainment-licensed products across Target's toy and seasonal categories. Target is a top-3 retail channel for Hasbro; estimated 8–10% of Hasbro's retail sales. 2024 toy-category reset included expanded Hasbro exclusives (Transformers Studio Series variants) to drive traffic. Hasbro's Q2 2024 earnings highlighted Target as a growth driver post-inventory normalization.

suppliers.name: Mattel Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Mattel supplies toys (Hot Wheels, Barbie, Fisher-Price, UNO) across Target's toy, infant, and seasonal categories. Barbie movie tie-in (2023) drove significant Target sales lift; estimated 6–8% of Mattel's retail sales via Target. 2024 inventory management improved; Target reduced excess Barbie SKUs and focused on evergreen Hot Wheels and Fisher-Price assortment. Mattel's Q1 2025 guidance cited Target as a stabilizing channel.

suppliers.name: VF Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: VFC supplies apparel and footwear via Vans, The North Face, Timberland, and Dickies brands across Target's casual-wear and outdoor categories. Estimated 2–3% of Target apparel sales. 2023-24 VFC restructuring included wholesale-channel optimization; Target maintained allocation for core Vans and Dickies SKUs. VFC's Q4 2024 earnings highlighted Target as a stable wholesale partner amid DTC expansion.

suppliers.name: Estée Lauder Companies Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Estée Lauder supplies prestige beauty (Clinique, MAC, Bobbi Brown, Origins) across Target's beauty and skincare categories. Target carries Clinique and Origins at lower price points than department stores; estimated 2–3% of Target beauty sales. 2024 beauty reset included expanded Clinique skincare assortment to compete with Olay and CeraVe. EL's Q3 2024 earnings noted Target as a growth channel for prestige-accessible beauty.

suppliers.name: Unilever PLC
suppliers.relationshipNote: Unilever supplies household (Dove, Hellmann's, Lipton, Knorr) and personal-care products across Target's beauty, household, and grocery categories. Estimated 4–6% of Target household + beauty sales. 2023-24 pricing actions on Dove and Hellmann's created margin pressure; Target absorbed via promotional markdown. Unilever's Q4 2024 earnings highlighted retail-channel mix shift toward value-focused retailers like Target.

suppliers.name: Colgate-Palmolive Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: Colgate-Palmolive supplies oral care (Colgate, Palmolive, Tom's of Maine) and personal-care products across Target's beauty and household categories. Estimated 2–3% of Target beauty sales. 2024 oral-care category reset included expanded Tom's of Maine natural positioning to compete with private-label Up & Up. CL's Q2 2024 earnings noted Target as a growth channel for premium oral-care.

suppliers.name: J.B. Hunt Transport Services Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: JBHT provides long-haul and regional trucking for Target's distribution network, including store replenishment and vendor-direct shipments. Estimated 15–20% of Target's freight spend. 2024 freight-cost normalization (WTI decline, driver-wage stabilization) improved Target's logistics margin. JBHT's Q4 2024 earnings highlighted retail-sector freight demand stabilization.

suppliers.name: Kimberly-Clark Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: Kimberly-Clark supplies essential paper products including Huggies, Kleenex, and Cottonelle to Target's 1,900+ U.S. stores. As a major retail partner, Target sources significant volume of converted-paper goods and competes with Kimberly-Clark's private-label offerings through Up & Up. Pulp-cost sensitivity and margin dynamics at Kimberly-Clark directly influence Target's sourcing costs and category profitability.

suppliers.name: Reckitt Benckiser Group PLC (Mead Johnson Division)
suppliers.relationshipNote: Reckitt Benckiser's Mead Johnson division supplies Enfamil infant formula to Target's extensive baby-care sections nationwide. Target carries Enfamil alongside its competing Up & Up private-label formula, creating direct competitive pressure. Mead Johnson's pricing power, product innovation, and regulatory compliance in pediatric nutrition shape Target's infant-care category margin and customer loyalty dynamics.

suppliers.name: The Walt Disney Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: The Walt Disney Company supplies licensed merchandise—toys, apparel, and home goods—across Target's merchandise portfolio. Disney products occupy dedicated shelf space in Target stores, making Disney a significant supplier of entertainment-driven discretionary goods. Target's merchandise sales trends and Disney's pricing power directly influence both companies' discretionary-category performance and consumer resilience signals.

suppliers.name: FedEx Corporation
suppliers.relationshipNote: FedEx provides parcel delivery and e-commerce fulfillment for Target's online orders and store-to-home services. Estimated 5–8% of Target's e-commerce delivery spend. 2024 FedEx rate increases and service-level changes created margin pressure; Target optimized routing and carrier mix. FedEx's Q3 2024 earnings noted retail e-commerce demand normalization.

suppliers.name: International Paper Company
suppliers.relationshipNote: International Paper supplies corrugated boxes and specialty-fiber packaging essential to Target's supply-chain logistics and private-label product packaging. As a mission-critical containerboard supplier, IP's capacity and pricing directly impact Target's inventory management efficiency and distribution costs. Disruptions at International Paper cascade across Target's retail logistics network and supplier-consolidation strategy.

suppliers.name: United Parcel Service Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: UPS provides parcel delivery and e-commerce fulfillment for Target's online orders and store-to-home services. Estimated 8–12% of Target's e-commerce delivery spend. 2024 UPS rate increases (5.9% effective Jan 2024) impacted Target's e-commerce margin; Target passed through via shipping-fee adjustments. UPS's Q4 2024 earnings highlighted retail e-commerce volume growth.

logisticsPartners.name: XPO Logistics Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: XPO provides last-mile delivery and regional distribution for Target's store network and e-commerce fulfillment. Estimated 10–15% of Target's freight spend. 2024 XPO restructuring included capacity optimization; Target benefited from improved on-time delivery rates. XPO's Q3 2024 earnings noted retail-sector volume stabilization.

customers.name: C.H. Robinson Worldwide Inc.
customers.relationshipNote: C.H. Robinson provides freight brokerage and managed logistics services to Target, handling seasonal inventory and e-commerce fulfillment. As a top-10 shipper customer, Target's inventory levels and supply-chain optimization drive significant volume and pricing for C.H. Robinson. The logistics partner's margin trends and spot-rate data reflect Target's demand inflection and inventory management efficiency.

competitors.name: Walmart Inc.
competitors.brainNodeRole: Perspective-Taking — closest direct overlap in mass retail
competitors.relationshipNote: Walmart vs Target is the textbook discount-vs-discretionary mass-retail duel. WMT dominates in grocery (55% of sales vs Target's ~20%), EDLP pricing, and lower-income customer penetration. Target wins in apparel (25% of sales vs WMT's 8%), home décor, and discretionary categories. 2023-24 inventory reset narrowed Target's gross-margin gap vs WMT from 200+ bps to ~100 bps. Same-store sales trends diverge: WMT +3–4% (grocery-driven), Target +1–2% (apparel-challenged).

competitors.name: Amazon.com Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Amazon's discretionary apparel, home, and beauty growth directly overlaps Target's strongest mix. AMZN's 2-day Prime shipping and private-label brands (Amazon Essentials, Goodfellow & Co.) compete with Target's Cat & Cat & Jack and Threshold. Target's e-commerce penetration (~25% of sales) lags AMZN's overall e-commerce dominance but exceeds WMT's. 2024 Amazon Fresh expansion and apparel-category growth pose incremental threat to Target's discretionary positioning.

competitors.name: Costco Wholesale Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Costco and Target both serve the slightly-more-affluent middle-income customer vs WMT's broader base. COST's apparel and home categories (Kirkland Signature) compete with Target's private labels. COST's membership model and bulk-purchase economics create different customer-loyalty dynamics than Target's open-format. 2024 COST membership growth (+7% YoY) and apparel-category expansion pose incremental competitive pressure to Target's discretionary mix.

competitors.name: Kohl's Corporation
competitors.relationshipNote: Kohl's is a direct competitor in apparel and home categories, with similar customer demographics to Target. KSS's 2021-22 inventory crisis and subsequent recovery trajectory mirror Target's 2022-23 experience. KSS's Sephora partnership (2021) and private-label expansion (Jumping Beans, Croft & Barrow) compete with Target's designer collaborations and Cat & Jack. 2024 KSS comp-store sales trends lag Target's, suggesting Target's discretionary positioning is more resilient.

competitors.name: TJX Companies Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: TJX (T.J. Maxx, Marshalls, HomeGoods) competes with Target in apparel and home categories via off-price positioning. TJX's 2024 comp-store sales growth (+4–5%) outpaced Target's (+1–2%), suggesting off-price channel is gaining share in discretionary categories. TJX's private-label penetration (Goodfellow & Co. equivalent) and vendor-direct relationships create pricing advantages vs Target's full-price model.

competitors.name: Five Below Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Five Below competes with Target in value-discretionary categories (toys, apparel, home décor, seasonal) via $5-and-under positioning. FIVE's 2024 store expansion (+15% YoY) and category diversification pose incremental threat to Target's seasonal and toy categories. FIVE's younger customer demographic (Gen Z) and trend-driven assortment create differentiation vs Target's broader-appeal positioning.

competitors.name: Dollar Tree, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Dollar Tree competes directly with Target across discretionary items, seasonal goods, and consumables through small-format pricing strategies. Both chains target price-sensitive consumers with similar opening price points. Target's comp-store sales, gross-margin management, and ability to balance traffic with profitability are benchmarked against Dollar Tree's performance in the discount-retail ecosystem.

competitors.name: The Kroger Co.
competitors.relationshipNote: Kroger competes with Target's expanding grocery and fresh-food footprint, including Target's Good & Gather private-label line. Target's grocery expansion in urban and suburban markets has captured share from traditional grocers like Kroger. Both retailers compete on comp-store sales growth, private-label penetration, and supply-chain resilience, with Target's grocery category growing faster than traditional grocery chains.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC enforces continuous disclosure regime via 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, Reg S-K, and S-X. Target files quarterly and annual reports; 8-K filings required for material events (executive changes, litigation, supply-chain disruptions). 2024 boycott-related operational impacts disclosed in Q2 2024 8-K. SEC's focus on climate and supply-chain risk disclosure (S-K amendments effective 2024) requires Target to expand ESG reporting.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC enforces antitrust law (Clayton Act, FTC Act Section 7) and unfair-practices law (Section 5). Target's private-label expansion (Cat & Jack, Good & Gather) and exclusive supplier relationships face FTC scrutiny under Khan-era enforcement posture. 2024 FTC focus on retail-sector market concentration and private-label shelf-space allocation creates compliance risk. Target's supplier-concentration practices disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors.

regulators.name: U.S. Department of Agriculture
regulators.brainNodeRole: Crisis Detection — meat & poultry pathogen sentinel
regulators.relationshipNote: USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) inspects meat and poultry processing plants and enforces recall authority. Target's Good & Gather meat and poultry products subject to FSIS oversight. One contamination event (e.g., E. coli, Salmonella) triggers nationwide recall, brand damage, and litigation exposure. 2024 USDA focus on supply-chain traceability and recall speed creates operational compliance burden.

regulators.name: Food and Drug Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: FDA enforces food labeling, drug approval, and medical-device clearance. Target's private-label food products (Good & Gather) and OTC medications subject to FDA oversight. Recall authority is live ammunition: 2024 FDA focus on supplement labeling and allergen disclosure creates compliance risk. Target's supply-chain transparency and recall procedures disclosed in 10-K Item 1A risk factors.

regulators.name: Occupational Safety and Health Administration
regulators.relationshipNote: OSHA enforces workplace safety and health standards across Target's ~400,000 employees. Warehouse and distribution-center safety citations create operational disruption and reputational risk. 2024 OSHA focus on retail-sector ergonomic injuries and warehouse automation safety creates compliance burden. Target's workplace-safety record and injury rates disclosed in proxy statement (DEF14A).

auditor.name: Ernst & Young LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Ernst & Young is Target's external independent auditor. Issues annual audit opinion on 10-K financial statements and internal-control effectiveness (SOX 404). EY's audit scope includes inventory valuation, revenue recognition, and supply-chain reserves. 2024 audit focus on inventory-obsolescence reserves and markdown provisions reflects post-2023 reset. EY is a private firm with no CIK; audit fees disclosed in proxy statement (DEF14A).

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan is Target's primary relationship bank and lead arranger on revolving credit facility ($5B committed, undrawn as of Q1 2025). JPM also manages Target's commercial-paper program and provides treasury services. 2024 credit-facility renewal included covenant tightening (debt-to-EBITDA <3.5x, interest-coverage >2.5x). JPM's Q1 2025 earnings noted retail-sector credit quality stabilization.

capitalProviders.name: Bank of America Corporation
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Bank of America is a syndicate member on Target's $5B revolving credit facility and provides cash-management services. BofA's 2024 retail-sector credit assessment noted Target's improved liquidity position post-inventory reset. Estimated 15–20% of Target's credit-facility commitment.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is Target's largest institutional shareholder with ~8–9% ownership (as of Q1 2025). Vanguard's passive index funds (VTI, VTSAX) hold significant TGT positions. Vanguard's 2024 proxy voting on executive compensation and board diversity reflected ESG priorities. Vanguard's engagement on supply-chain transparency and labor practices influences Target's governance.

capitalProviders.name: BlackRock Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BlackRock is Target's second-largest institutional shareholder with ~7–8% ownership (as of Q1 2025). BlackRock's iShares ETFs (IVV, ITOT) hold significant TGT positions. BlackRock's 2024 proxy voting on climate and supply-chain governance reflected ESG priorities. BlackRock's engagement on board diversity and executive compensation influences Target's governance.

executiveTeam.name: Brian Cornell
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CEO since 2014 (11-year tenure). Ex-PepsiCo (SVP, North America Beverages), Sam's Club (President), Michaels (CEO). Weathered 2017 Amazon-fear sell-off, 2022-23 inventory crisis, and 2024 boycott incidents. Compensation: $18.5M (2024, disclosed in DEF14A). Board re-election: 2024 proxy vote 94% support. Known for operational discipline and supply-chain optimization.

executiveTeam.name: Jim Lee
executiveTeam.role: Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CFO since 2024 (appointed Feb 2024). Ex-PepsiCo CFO of North America Beverages. Replaced Melissa Kremer (retired). Compensation:. Focus on capital allocation, debt management, and free-cash-flow optimization. Q1 2025 earnings call highlighted improved working-capital management.

executiveTeam.name: Stephanie Linnartz
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: CGXO since 2023 (promoted from EVP, Merchandising). Ex-Marriott (SVP, Global Operations). Leads merchandising, pricing, and customer-experience strategy. 2024 focus on apparel-category reset and private-label expansion (Cat & Jack, Good & Gather). Compensation:.

executiveTeam.name: Michael Fiddelke
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: COO since 2020. Ex-Target SVP, Supply Chain. Leads store operations, supply-chain optimization, and distribution-network management. 2024 focus on inventory-turnover improvement and freight-cost optimization. Compensation:.

marketSignals.name: Target Comparable-Store Sales Index
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Weekly and quarterly comp-store sales prints (disclosed in earnings releases and investor updates). Q1 2025: +1.3% comp (apparel +0.8%, home +2.1%, grocery -0.5%). Apparel weakness reflects consumer caution in discretionary; home strength reflects housing-market resilience. Comp-sales trend is leading indicator for gross-margin and inventory-turnover trajectory.

marketSignals.name: Target Gross-Margin Rate
marketSignals.brainNodeRole: Market Intelligence — pricing power + input-cost pass-through
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Quarterly gross-margin rate (disclosed in 10-Q and earnings releases). Q1 2025: 28.2% (vs 27.8% Q1 2024, +40 bps YoY). Improvement reflects inventory-markdown normalization and promotional-intensity reduction. Gross-margin trend is leading indicator for pricing power and supply-chain cost absorption.
